approach.method_basis: The Parent constructs fresh graph-edited offspring from accepted scored parents, then uses an accepted-feedback fingerprint Gaussian process and correlated posterior draws to select each batch. Candidate strings also serve as the keys for temporary uniqueness, emitted exclusions and matching later scores. Its graph checker returns a reparsed molecule with the spelling produced just before that parse, which can leave the stored graph and its identity key out of step.
approach.novelty: Require a stable molecular identity before a candidate enters the pool. Keep already consistent identities, normalize a changing spelling only when the new spelling survives confirmation and still describes the original checked graph, and reject representations that remain inconsistent through the existing bounded generation loop. Earlier siblings altered chemical edits or parent allocation. This change leaves the generated graph and selector intact and extends an earlier identity-repair idea to the newly observed case of alternating representations.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's checked_molecule serializes a cleaned graph, parses that string and returns the parsed molecule together with the earlier string. The pool therefore can store a molecule whose next canonical serialization differs from its identity key. A read-only audit of all 69,600 Parent pool records finds exactly two such aliases, both in seed-1 deco_hop batch 27 at pool indices 120 and 149. Each normalizes to a spelling that is stable on confirmation, with equal atom/bond counts, mutual chiral graph matches and identical inherited Morgan fingerprints. Neither was emitted, and no normalized pool/global-seen collisions were found on the recorded panel. The completed carbonyl sibling demonstrates a more serious limit of simple renaming: among its 69,600 pool records, 61 change on another parse/serialize, and 59 of those still change on confirmation. One of its 4,350 actual emissions is such an unstable pure-crossover product. The extra parsed representation changes the inherited fingerprint for 54 of the 61 changing pool records, including the emitted case; equal atom and bond counts therefore do not establish an unchanged represented graph. All recorded tasks completed, so this evidence does not claim an observed lookup crash in this Parent or sibling. A previous lineage's parse-and-reserialize repair resolved a stable alias, but did not establish admission safety for representations that alternate on repeated parsing. This Child addresses generated-pool molecule/identity agreement and bounded rejection of unresolved representations, not chemical quality or a predicted score gain.
hypothesis: Admit generated pool candidates only under a parse-and-serialize-stable canonical identity, normalizing stable aliases and rejecting representations that remain inconsistent on confirmation.

finding_summary.headline: Two pool identities stabilized; every evaluated molecule and score stayed unchanged
finding_summary.insights: This establishes a correction at the pool interface that preserves the represented graphs and the search trajectory under the installed parser. Its demonstrated benefit is stable bookkeeping: the only corrected entries were unselected, and their fingerprints were unchanged. A separate read-only replay rejected all 59 unstable representations recorded in the sibling with carbonyl preservation, including one that sibling had emitted. Five of those unstable representations retained the same fingerprint after another parse, showing why fingerprint equality cannot substitute for the registered identity test. The child itself produced no unstable candidate and never evaluated a renamed identity, so empirical failure prevention and accepted feedback under a changed key remain open. Its unchanged emitted chemistry still contains reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide bonds, concentrated aromatic ring families and unspecified stereochemistry. Identity consistency does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results: Both known stable aliases were normalized, reducing disagreements between stored pool identities and their molecules from two to zero. Across 75,484 otherwise valid checked attempts, 75,482 identities stayed unchanged and two received confirmed spellings of the same graphs. Independent checks found no admitted identity instability, graph modification, new identity collision or feedback mismatch. Neither corrected pool member was selected. All 435 pools reached 160 candidates, and all 4,350 generated evaluations retained the parent’s exact molecule and score order. Mean final-best score across three seeds remained 0.544374, with population standard deviation 0.013310; every paired task and seed score difference was zero, within the supplied 0.002 non-inferiority allowance. The offspring parent-beating rate also stayed at 565 of 4,350, or 12.99%. Identity checks consumed 7.28 seconds in aggregate, and the added receipts increased diagnostic log size from 98.24 MB to 147.13 MB. Recorded total wall time was lower, but these historical runs do not isolate the incremental runtime cost.

molecular.headline: Parent chemistry persists: aromatic polycycles, halogenated amines and carbonyl heterocycles, with reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The evaluated molecule/score order matches Parent n-fc2c108a5253 in every supplied task/seed trajectory. The emitted chemistry therefore remains the same. All objectives have trajectories; each digest covers 900 molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. This is a ring-rich, mostly aromatic output with several distinct seed-dependent families: compact bridged heterocycles, linked carbonyl heteroaromatics, aryl-substituted saturated amines, and larger aza rings. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9736 to 0.9943 and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.9414 to 0.9885. These are fractions of SMILES containing the indicated text features, not fractions of atoms or measured ring counts. Both the charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0 throughout. Neutral SMILES still contain potentially basic amines, and the lack of stereochemical labels does not mean the graphs are achiral. Recognizable medicinal chemistry fragments coexist with oxygen-halogen bonds, nitrogen-halogen bonds, peroxide chains, crowded aminal centres, unusual ring junctions, and occasional very small or extensively concatenated products. Structural diversity is moderate across the full panel but much narrower within the highest-scoring excerpts. Synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly absent: familiar substructures are present, while complete routes, stability, and stereochemical control are not established. The score-gradient statements below describe associations in the supplied molecules and scores; they do not establish an unseen target structure, experimentally measured activity, or an intrinsic score benefit from repairing a chemical liability.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are compact but densely fused or bridged aromatic heterocycles carrying an aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl appendage and small alkyl substituents. The leading structure has an ethyl/methyl-substituted nitrogen-containing polycycle with an O-methylene bridge and a ketone connected through methylene to fluoropyridine. Other high examples replace that connection with an aroyl group or a thioester. The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide is recognizable conventional chemistry; later structures also include N-fluoro amides and fused N-N or N-O rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.5, with ring-closure rate 0.9736, aromatic presence 0.9724, and halogen presence 0.869. These are mostly substantial multi-ring molecules, with small fragment outliers. The leading ketone is more chemically interpretable than some heteroatom-rich variants, but its unusual bridged core would still need a credible synthesis and structural assignment. Chemistry and associated scores are unchanged from the Parent.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides, N-N/N-O ring linkages, and a thioester introduce different reactivity or stability concerns; they should not be treated as interchangeable examples of ordinary aryl fluorination or amide chemistry.
Unusual short bridges and ring junctions complicate synthetic planning and geometry, while the SMILES provide no explicit stereochemical specification.
Ethene and the N-chloro imine demonstrate loss of essentially the entire multi-ring feature combination even late in the trajectory.
missing_features: The low-scoring fragment products lack the aromatic/heteroaromatic surfaces and carbonyl-bearing connection jointly present in the higher-scoring molecules.

The output does not establish broad, synthetically routine alternative cores that retain this compact feature arrangement; the best excerpt stays close to an unusual bridged family. An additional unseen target-specific group cannot be inferred from the observed scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the leading bridged heterocycle/fluoropyridyl ketone scores 0.4463521672202675. The high aroyl analogue scores 0.4349635367667153, and the thioester analogue still scores 0.4238198477630873. The common observed association is a compact aromatic carbonyl-bearing assembly with small substituents, not one uniquely established linker chemistry. The late N-fluoro-amide/N-N-ring product scores 0.3630045684864706, whereas the final ethene and the N-chloro imine fragment score 0.0. Ring-free fragments do not express the combination retained by the better molecules. These comparisons do not establish that added bridges, thioesters, or N-halogen bonds are independently beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules join carbonyl-bearing O/N heteroaromatic ring systems through an NH connection. The leading family also carries an aryl cyanate substituent, a short annulated carbon bridge, an aryl halogen, and an O-O-Cl chain. The final excerpt contains still more nitrogen-rich fused/linked dicarbonyl heterocycles, including N-F, N-Cl, and oxygen-chlorine substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 94.4 and the maximum is 248: the full trajectories include much larger concatenated aromatic assemblies than the leading compact representatives. Ring-closure and aromatic presence are both 0.9885; halogen presence is 0.7851. The familiar carbonyl heterocycles and NH linkage are embedded in molecules whose reactive substituents and complex annulation make overall synthetic plausibility questionable. The Parent has the same chemistry and score order.
liabilities: O-O-Cl and O-O-F chains combine peroxide and oxygen-halogen bonds; these are chemical reactivity liabilities despite their high objective scores.
Late N-halogenated dicarbonyl heterocycles and oxygen-halogen substituents raise further stability and synthetic-handling concerns.
Short annulated bridges, extensively repeated heterocyclic units, and large aromatic surfaces complicate synthesis and molecular properties; SMILES validity alone does not resolve those concerns.
missing_features: The tiny low-scoring molecules lack the linked aromatic surfaces, NH connection, and distributed carbonyl/heteroatom acceptors present in the higher-scoring family.

The highest excerpt poorly covers chemically ordinary replacements for the unusual peripheral bonds while preserving the same compact core geometry. The fluoromethyl example shows one such alternative; the scores do not identify a required unvisited scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623, compared with 0.6324703199409752 for the leading linked heteroaromatic product. Small methylamine and molecular chlorine examples both score 0.5, so that floor does not demonstrate useful molecular features. Within a closely related high-scoring core, the O-O-Cl-bearing structure scores 0.6300605077662029 and the fluoromethyl replacement scores 0.6293992623616929. Replacing its aryl bromine with methyl retains 0.6300605077662029. Thus the observed score is compatible with the linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement while distinguishing these reactive or halogen substituents only weakly. It does not establish a need for peroxide-halogen chemistry or increasing molecular size.

per_task.generated_character: The better products are medium-sized aryl-rich amines with saturated nitrogen-containing rings and flexible benzylic or alkenyl connections. One high-scoring family contains a saturated diaza ring with a crowded aminal centre, an exocyclic amine, an N-alkyl substituent, and substituted aromatic ends. Another has spiro-connected aza rings, halogenated aryl groups, and an aryl thiol. Mean proposal SMILES length is 60.2; ring-closure presence is 0.9851, aromatic presence 0.9782, and halogen presence 0.9874. These molecules already contain basic-amine opportunities; a lack of ring nitrogens is not their general limitation. Some spiro-amine frameworks are recognizable medicinal chemistry, while the crowded aminals, occasional O-Cl groups, chloromethyl substituents and undefined stereochemistry make the full products less routine. The same structures and scores occur in the Parent.
liabilities: Crowded aminal centres, including a carbon bearing an exocyclic amino group and both ring nitrogens, require scrutiny for stability and synthetic accessibility.
Aryl thiols, O-Cl substituents, and N-chloromethyl groups occur alongside otherwise recognizable amine frameworks; high scores do not establish their suitability.
No explicit charge or stereochemical labels are present. Potentially basic nitrogens are encoded neutrally, so the emitted strings do not document a protonation-state or stereoisomer exploration.
missing_features: Low-scoring aryl fragments and the final truncated aminal fail to retain the aromatic-appendage/amine/geometry combination expressed by the better molecules.

The spiro and substituted saturated-ring products lack stereochemical specification. Their graphs can encode different spatial arrangements, but the trajectories do not test whether a particular stereoisomer improves this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminal/aryl/amine assembly scores 0.9914038363125457 and the spiro-amine/aryl-thiol example 0.9908331648929692. A small halogenated aromatic fragment scores 0.001421581552029289. A particularly useful local comparison retains the aryl ends and enamine-linked core: the ring N-methyl analogue scores 0.981088217863691, while its N-formyl analogue scores 0.48797702544581545. That change alters nitrogen electronics and hydrogen-bonding capacity. The final smaller product retaining the diaza ring and fluorinated aromatic end but losing the other aromatic appendage scores 0.011495655106721757. The visible gradient favors the combined aromatic surface, amine character, and connecting geometry. It does not imply that every amine, extra halogen, or additional nitrogen independently helps.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are medium-to-large cyclic assemblies containing alkyl-substituted pyridyl or quinolyl groups, a benzofused carbonyl heterocycle, and N-methylated aza rings or macrocyclic connections. Carbonyls, aromatic nitrogens, tertiary amines or amidic nitrogens recur; oxygen and sulfur substitutions appear among neighboring products. The final excerpt includes unsaturated, nitrogen-rich larger rings bearing quinoline-like appendages. Mean proposal SMILES length is 55.9; ring-closure presence is 0.9943, aromatic presence 0.9885, and halogen presence only 0.269. This family is much less dependent on halogen decoration than the others. The individual functional groups are often familiar, but constructing the complete fused/bridged larger-ring arrangements would require deliberate synthetic planning and stereochemical control. Chemistry and its score trajectory remain identical to the Parent.
liabilities: Large and sometimes bridged aza rings create conformational and ring-closure challenges; their existence as valid graphs is not a synthesis.
Serial changes interconvert tertiary amines, amides and urea-like connections, changing basicity and donor/acceptor patterns along with ring geometry.
Bulky repeated aromatic appendages and unspecified stereochemistry add uncertainty even though this family has fewer obvious heteroatom-halogen liabilities than several other outputs.
missing_features: Low-scoring chains lack the coupled heteroaromatic/carbonyl/cyclic-nitrogen arrangement that is present in the better products.

The highest excerpt provides limited alternative, synthetically straightforward ring topologies retaining that feature arrangement, and it does not specify stereochemistry at newly substituted or bridged centres. The observed scores do not identify a particular missing target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329, whereas the leading pyridyl/benzofused dicarbonyl/aza-ring assembly scores 0.22405709718343647. A related analogue without the extra methylene between the N-methyl nitrogen and carbonyl scores 0.21884002370946612; this changes both ring size and amine-versus-amidic character, so those effects cannot be separated. Ethane scores 0.012461119656980673 and the small acyclic amide 0.025605696979529788. The common higher-scoring feature set is the combined aromatic heterocycle, nitrogen-rich ring and carbonyl arrangement, rather than amide presence alone. The larger final molecule carrying repeated quinoline-like appendages scores 0.1754730092490373, below the more compact final dicarbonyl aza-ring example at 0.21037674112349405; repetition and size alone do not ensure higher score.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of compact fluorinated aryl compounds attached to an N-alkylated fused dicarbonyl heterocycle, with aminomethyl or aminoethyl substituents. The top example has a free primary amine, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl groups, and the carbonyl-bearing heterocycle; neighboring examples include N-F substitution. Another seed finishes with more extensively fused heteroaromatics bearing thiol/hydroxyl groups and small fluorinated carbocycles, without the same pendant primary amine. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.0, ring-closure presence 0.9747, aromatic presence 0.9414, and halogen presence 0.7172. The cumulated-double-bond text rate is 0.0483, so such bonds are a minority feature rather than the dominant chemistry. The leading aminomethyl compound contains comparatively conventional functional groups; N-fluoro congeners, very large repeated cores and unsaturated small rings elsewhere are less straightforward. The Parent emits the same chemistry with the same scores.
liabilities: N-F substitution on carbonyl heterocycles is chemically distinct from ordinary C-F substitution and introduces a reactivity concern despite high scores.
Small unsaturated carbocycles, thiol substituents and cumulated-double-bond examples require chemical scrutiny; these are not evidence of an intrinsically inaccessible whole output.
Large repeated heterocyclic/aromatic assemblies show that the emitted chemistry does not reliably remain within the compact size and feature balance seen in the better family.
missing_features: The very low-scoring repeated polyaryl products and the late fused thiol family do not reproduce the compact primary-amine/fluorinated-aryl/dicarbonyl arrangement expressed by the leading family.

The output lacks a broad set of chemically stable scaffold alternatives preserving that arrangement. Where small saturated carbocycles create stereochemical choices, these are unspecified; a stereochemical score benefit has not been demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl/dicarbonyl compound scores 0.5845583988949146. Its close aryl-chloro analogue scores 0.5064928497454653: replacing that aryl chlorine with fluoromethyl accompanies an increase within this particular family. A related aminoethyl compound containing N-F still scores 0.5652209810580261, so the objective does not automatically exclude that chemical liability. The bulky repeated dicarbonyl/polyaryl product scores 1.6758614448245604e-53, whereas the compact initial dicarbonyl/aryl molecule scores 0.0020944534688323298. Mere possession of this heterocycle or increasing its copy number is insufficient. The late fused, thiol-bearing fluorocarbocycle product scores 0.4071395189354175, while its much smaller final fused relative scores 0.0038179150668162477. Several features change together, so a unique causal group cannot be assigned. The strongest visible family combines a bounded scaffold, a primary amine and particular fluorinated substituents; exact unseen pharmacophore requirements are not established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading molecule, Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(OOCl)c5c(Br)cc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1, contains an O-O-Cl chain; CCc1c(F)c(CCN)cc(-n2cc3c(c2F)c(=O)n(F)c(=O)n3CF)c1F contains N-F on a dicarbonyl heterocycle. Closely related peroxide-halogen and fluoromethyl products receive 0.6300605077662029 and 0.6293992623616929, so the observed feedback can distinguish stable-looking and reactive peripheral chemistry only weakly.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain conventional functional-group chemistry when adding heteroatoms or halogens.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically interpretable local substitutions that preserve functional-group roles and distinguish carbon-halogen bonds from oxygen-halogen, nitrogen-halogen and peroxide linkages. Evaluate this as a general property of generated chemistry; no objective-specific substituent list is supported.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0, yet Cc1cc(Br)cc(Cl)c1C1CNCC12CCN(C(C)c1cccc(S)c1)C2 has substituted spiro aza-ring geometry and CC1C(F)C1c1c2c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n(C)c2c2c3nc(O)c(c(CS)c3F)n12 has a substituted saturated small carbocycle. The absence of stereochemical labels is an observed coverage gap, not evidence that a particular stereoisomer would score better.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not represent stereochemical alternatives for its substituted, spiro and bridged saturated structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information and support chemically consistent stereochemical specification when a generated graph introduces such choices. Use the same chemistry rules and feedback process for every objective, with consistent isomeric identity handling.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The ring N-methyl molecule C=C(NC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F scores 0.981088217863691; its N-formyl analogue C=C(NC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C=O)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F scores 0.48797702544581545. A final smaller analogue missing an aromatic appendage, C=C(CNO)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F, scores 0.011495655106721757. The useful chemistry is a combined arrangement rather than the presence of nitrogen alone.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve useful amine electronics and aromatic appendages together while varying a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make local alternatives that can retain ring topology, aromatic appendages and amine class while varying a limited chemical feature, and separately expose deliberate changes of amine to amide character. Let observed feedback determine which combinations matter without assigning task identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set has mean SMILES length 94.4 and maximum 248. Other supplied records include the very large repeated-core molecule Cn1c(=O)c2c(-c3ccccc3)n(-c3cc4cc(c3O)C(n3c(=O)c5c(-c6ccccc6)n(-c6cc(C(=O)OCCl)ccc6O)cc5n(C)c3=O)OC4=O)cc2n(C)c1=O at 1.6758614448245604e-53, and the final fragment C=C at 0.0. The higher-scoring excerpts instead retain connected combinations of aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl features. These observations do not establish a universal preferred size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry does not reliably maintain a bounded multi-feature molecular size across structural changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support changes that retain a coherent connected set of chemical features without either duplicating whole aromatic assemblies or stripping down to tiny fragments. Size control should depend on general molecular structure and available score feedback, not a fixed objective-specific formula or size target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading excerpts repeatedly vary the bridged carbonyl scaffold CCc1cc2c3cc(C(=O)Cc4ccc(F)cn4)n2COc1c3C, the short-annulated linked heteroaromatics Cc1cc2oc(=O)nc(Nc3c4c(OOCl)c5c(Br)cc(=O)oc5c3C4)c2c(OC#N)n1, or the larger aza-ring assembly CCCc1nc(C2CCCN(C)CC(=O)n3c(=O)cc2c2ccccc23)ccc1CC. The digest shows abundant ring and aromatic text features, so missing rings are not the problem; topology and chemically coherent alternatives within each successful feature arrangement are the narrower coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring output gives limited coverage of ordinary alternative core geometries around the same useful functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable coordinated core changes that preserve recognizable donor, acceptor and potentially basic-amine arrangements while exploring alternative accessible ring connections. Assess the resulting chemistry and feedback rather than equating additional ring closures or unique SMILES with broader useful scaffold coverage.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
Local atom/bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph-based retries for complete novel pools; saturation-dependent retry branches retained but not exercised
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

Accepted-only task-local fingerprint Gaussian-process archive, exact joint posterior sampling over fresh offspring pools, masked batch selection, and feedback-driven posterior refitting; bounded numerical fallback retained but not exercised

Pool-only stable canonical identity admission: copy serialization, confirmed graph-equivalent alias normalization retaining the original checked molecule, and bounded rejection of unresolved representations; rejection exercised only on historical records, not formal child proposals
